items.prompt: Why must a partition used for total probability be exhaustive as well as disjoint?

options.text: Disjoint events automatically cover every outcome
options.why: They can leave outcomes outside the listed groups.

options.text: Every likelihood must be numerically identical
options.why: Different groups can have different likelihoods.

options.text: It prevents probabilities from ever depending on assumptions
options.why: The probabilities still come from a model.

options.text: Otherwise the denominator omits unlisted evidence mass
options.why: Missing groups can make the calculated posterior wrong.

items.explanation: Summing only part of the population is not the full evidence probability unless omitted groups contribute no mass under a justified model.
